events.label: Post-collapse future Director governs remnant humanity
events.description: Centuries from now, humanity's remnant huddles in grim bunkers after catastrophe, governed by an intelligence called the Director that rations everything, including hope.

events.label: Consciousness transfer into historical hosts at death moments
events.description: The Director saves dying people of the past by overwriting a doomed host's mind with a traveller's consciousness at the instant of death - a transfer no one survives without a body to catch them.

events.label: Team 3412 arrives in 21st-century host bodies
events.description: A five-person team arrives in 21st-century bodies - an FBI agent, a counsellor, a student, a young mother, and an opioid-addicted young man - and must find each other using coded phrases.

events.label: Missions avert disasters per Director protocols
events.description: Following numbered protocols, the team carries out missions that avert disasters - assassinations, outbreaks, catastrophes - each one nudging history away from the collapse they came from.

events.label: Faction seeks to rewrite future against Director
events.description: A breakaway faction of travellers decides the Director's plans are wrong and works to rewrite the future on their own terms, turning time's refugees against each other.

events.label: Host families complicate Traveler ethics
events.description: Every traveller inherits a host's unfinished life - a marriage, a baby, an addiction - and keeping those lives afloat while saving the world is the show's moral engine.

events.label: Protocol overrides and Helo/antiviral stakes escalate
events.description: The Director can seize any traveller's body at any moment with an override, and as its schemes grow more ruthless - engineered viruses, impossible demands - obedience turns into resistance.

events.label: Director's continuity vs human agency conflict
events.description: The conflict at the heart of the story: the Director's cold calculations versus the travellers' own conscience - is humanity's future worth humanity's freedom?

events.label: Final missions attempt to stabilize best available future
events.description: In the final series, the team runs out of clean options and makes desperate plays - new protocols, hard sacrifices - to land on the best future still within reach.

events.label: Host deaths / Traveler losses as transfer cost
events.description: The programme's price is human: hosts die so travellers can arrive, and travellers die on missions - every rescue in the past is paid for by someone.

events.label: Future updates based on mission outcomes (bootstrap intel)
events.description: The future watches the present: historians record outcomes and send updates back, so each mission's results shape the next set of instructions - the past and future coaching each other.

events.label: Series ends with hard-won, still-fragile continuum
events.description: The series ends without a bow: the worst futures may be averted, but what remains is a fragile, hard-won world still full of damage - and the team simply carries on.

events.label: Historians in future monitor divergence
events.description: In the future, historians monitor how the past drifts from the record, flagging divergences so the Director can adjust its plans accordingly.

events.label: Traveler consciousness into host
events.description: A traveller's mind is beamed into the body of a person about to die, so the future can act in the past without changing its own birth.

events.label: Director AI missions
events.description: The Director - part archive, part artificial intelligence - hands down numbered protocols and missions, managing the past like a garden it needs to survive.

events.label: Team macros in present
events.description: The team works in cells with codenames and macros, finding each other in the present with handshakes and coded phrases before taking on missions together.

events.label: Faction conflict
events.description: Some travellers come to believe they know better than the Director, and their rebellion sets traveller against traveller across the present day.

events.label: Host consciousness ethics
events.description: Overwriting a host's mind with a traveller's raises the show's hardest question: whose life is it now, and what does the traveller owe the person they replaced?

events.label: Missions rewrite future disasters
events.description: Every disaster the team averts rewrites the future they came from - saving the world, one catastrophe at a time, with no guarantee history will thank them.

events.label: Grand plan revisions
events.description: The Director's grand plan keeps shifting as outcomes come in, and the team must revise its loyalties each time the goalposts move.

events.label: Series end stakes
events.description: By the end, the stakes are no longer one mission but the shape of the future itself - and the travellers, not the Director, are the ones holding it.

ruleEffects.effect: Past interventions rewrite future conditions the Director updates against
Mission intel and programs bootstrap from outcomes they create

outcome.summary: Travelers rewrite collapse trajectory under Director protocols; ethics of host lives and AI governance remain central; continuum fragile but improved.
